docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The team is developing a lunar rover as part of a Lunar Digital Twin project using Unity and Virtual Reality (VR).

docs.title: Rover Components
docs.text: The rover consists of a main body, four wheels, and solar panels. These components are represented in the Unity environment.

docs.title: Movement and Navigation
docs.text: The rover is designed to move across the simulated lunar surface. The team is working on wheel movement, traction, rover physics, and navigation.

docs.title: Lunar Environment Interaction
docs.text: The rover must interact with the lunar terrain and avoid obstacles such as rocks. Collision detection is used to prevent the rover from passing through the terrain or environmental objects.

docs.title: Development Goals
docs.text:
• Develop a functional rover model.
  • Simulate realistic rover movement.
  • Improve interaction with lunar terrain.
  • Integrate the rover into the virtual lunar environment.

docs.title: 💻 Rutgers University – Software Development and Digital Twin
🔵 Introduction
docs.text:
The Rutgers University team was responsible for developing the software and virtual components of the NASA Lunar Rover Digital Twin project. Our work focused on creating a virtual lunar environment and developing the software systems needed to represent, monitor, and interact with the rover.

The goal was to bring together software development, digital twin technology, autonomous navigation, and Virtual Reality (VR) to create an interactive lunar exploration experience.

docs.title: ⚙️ Our Work and Contributions
docs.text:
Throughout the project, the Rutgers team worked on several important areas:

  • 🌐 Virtual Lunar Environment: Developed a lunar surface environment in Unity using Cesium, adding terrain, rocks, stations, solar panels, and other environmental elements to create a more realistic exploration setting.

  • 💻 Digital Twin Development: Worked on the virtual representation of the rover and the connection between the physical rover and its digital counterpart.

  • 🧭 Rover Navigation: Worked on pathfinding functionality using the A* algorithm to help the virtual rover identify routes and navigate through the lunar environment.

  • 📊 Rover Monitoring and Interface: Developed user interface features to display rover information, monitor its status, and communicate important system information.

  • 🥽 Virtual Reality Development: Worked on creating an immersive VR experience that allows users to explore and interact with the virtual lunar environment.

docs.title: 🤝 Team Collaboration
docs.text:
The Rutgers team worked collaboratively, with members contributing to different software components and development tasks. Through teamwork, testing, and integration, we brought together the virtual environment, rover systems, navigation features, and user interface into a shared project.

Each contribution helped move the project closer to its overall goal of creating an interactive digital twin of a lunar rover.

docs.title: 🏆 Rutgers Team Accomplishments
docs.text:
Our work represents an important part of the overall project. We developed the foundation of the virtual lunar environment, implemented software features, and worked toward connecting the physical rover with its digital representation.

These accomplishments demonstrate our progress in software engineering, problem-solving, system integration, and collaborative development.

The result is a virtual platform designed to support lunar rover exploration and provide an immersive experience through digital twin and VR technology.

docs.text: This section explains how to set up the software development environment for the Lunar Rover Digital Twin project.

docs.title: Required Software
docs.text:
The following tools are used for project development:

  • Unity Hub: Used to manage Unity installations and projects.
  • Unity Editor: Used to develop and run the lunar rover simulation.
  • Git: Used for version control and tracking project changes.
  • GitHub: Used to share project files and collaborate with team members.
  • Cesium for Unity: Used to create and integrate the lunar environment.

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text:
1. Install Unity Hub.
  2. Install the Unity Editor version used by the team.
  3. Clone the team's GitHub repository.
  4. Open the Unity project through Unity Hub.
  5. Allow Unity to import the project assets and packages.
  6. Open the lunar environment scene.
  7. Press Play in Unity to run the simulation.

docs.title: Development Tools
docs.text:

GitHub is used to manage project updates and collaborate across the development team.

docs.text: Team members should use the same Unity Editor version and project packages to maintain compatibility.

docs.title: 🚀 Overview
docs.text:
The A* (A-Star) Pathfinding Algorithm is used to help the lunar rover find an efficient route between a starting position and a destination.

The goal is to adapt A* for lunar navigation by considering terrain elevation, obstacles, slopes, and travel distance.

docs.title: ⚙️ How A* Works
docs.text:
The algorithm evaluates possible routes using movement costs and estimated remaining distance to find a suitable path.

The process includes:

  • 📍 Starting Point: Identifies the rover's current position.
  • 🎯 Destination: Defines where the rover needs to go.
  • 🗺️ Terrain Analysis: Examines elevation, slopes, and obstacles.
  • 🔍 Path Search: Compares possible routes using movement costs.
  • 🛣️ Route Selection: Finds an efficient route to the destination.

docs.title: 🌕 Terrain Data Acquisition
docs.text:
Cesium for Unity is used as the source of lunar terrain data.

The terrain sampling process includes:

  • Collecting latitude, longitude, and elevation information.
  • Selecting a sampling location near the lunar south pole (88°S).
  • Using terrain data with approximately 5-meter-per-pixel resolution.
  • Sampling neighboring grid locations to build terrain information.

docs.title: 🧩 Graph Generation
docs.text:
The terrain is converted into a graph made of nodes and edges.

  • Nodes: Represent individual terrain grid positions.
  • Edges: Represent possible movements between neighboring nodes.
  • 8-Connected Grid: Allows movement in eight directions, including horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions.
  • Edge Costs: Consider distance, slope, traversability, and estimated energy consumption.
  • Blocked Paths: Unsafe or blocked movements are excluded from the graph.

docs.title: 🔋 Terrain Costs and Energy Considerations
docs.text:
The pathfinding system considers different factors when evaluating possible routes.

  • 📏 Distance: Measures the distance between nodes.
  • ⛰️ Slope: Considers changes in terrain elevation.
  • 🚧 Obstacles: Identifies movements that may not be safe.
  • ⚡ Energy: Estimates the energy required to travel along a route.

These factors help the algorithm select a route that is suitable for lunar rover navigation.

docs.title: 📊 Current Progress
docs.text:
The project has made progress in developing the terrain data and graph-generation components.

  • Cesium for Unity has been integrated as the source of terrain data.
  • Terrain sampling methods have been developed.
  • The graph-generation approach uses an 8-connected grid.
  • Edge costs are designed to account for terrain conditions and estimated energy use.

Further work includes completing pathfinding integration and testing the system with the rover.

docs.title: 🔮 Future Improvements for the Next Team
docs.text:
The next team can continue developing the pathfinding system by focusing on:

  • 🛣️ Completing A* implementation and connecting it to the rover.
  • 🗺️ Improving terrain analysis and obstacle detection.
  • 🔋 Developing battery and energy consumption modeling.
  • 🎯 Adding destination selection and automatic route planning.
  • 🧪 Testing different routes to evaluate safety and algorithm performance.
  • 🔄 Improving communication between the pathfinding algorithm, Unity environment, and rover system.

The long-term goal is to create a reliable navigation system that allows the rover to select and follow suitable routes across the lunar surface.

docs.title: 🖥️ Rover UI
docs.text: The Rover UI provides an interface for monitoring rover information and managing mission tasks within the LunarSouthPole_Cesium Unity scene. It includes rover status displays, mission planning controls, and desktop and VR interfaces.

docs.title: 📊 Rover Status Display
docs.text:
The RoverStatusUI.cs script displays important rover information, including:

  • Status: Shows whether the rover is Online or in Standby.
  • Position: Displays the rover's X, Y, and Z coordinates.
  • Speed: Displays the rover's speed in meters per second.
  • Heading: Shows the rover's direction in degrees.
  • Mission Progress: Displays the current mission status.

The status display starts in Standby, and the mission progress starts as Not Started.

docs.title: 🎮 Mission Controls
docs.text:
The interface includes controls for managing the rover's mission:

  • Start Mission: Changes the rover status to Online and displays In Progress.
  • Pause Mission: Changes the rover status to Standby and displays Paused.
  • Reset Mission: Stops the rover's movement, returns it to its starting position and rotation, and resets the mission status to Not Started.

docs.title: 📋 Mission Planning Interface
docs.text:
The MissionPlanningUI.cs script provides an interface for selecting and assigning rover tasks.

Users can select from four available tasks:

  • Find Water
  • Collect Water
  • Deposit Water at Tank
  • Return to Base

The selected tasks appear in the Assigned Tasks section. If no tasks are selected, the interface displays "No tasks selected."

docs.title: 🗺️ Route Overview and Mission Progress
docs.text:
The interface includes a Route Overview that displays the planned destinations based on the selected tasks.

The route can include:

  • Base Camp
  • Water Search Area
  • Water Collection Site
  • Water Tank

The Mission Progress section provides a place to display mission status and updates. The interface also uses a page switcher to display the mission progress page when a mission is submitted.

docs.title: 🚀 Mission Assignment
docs.text:
The Assign Mission button prepares a mission request using the selected tasks and route information.

Before submission, the system checks the communication connection and requires recorded-data test mode. It also uses mission acknowledgments to receive information about whether a mission request was accepted.

The assignment button is disabled when no tasks are selected or while waiting for an acknowledgment.

docs.title: 🔄 Desktop and VR Interface
docs.text:
The Rover UI supports both desktop and VR displays.

The RoverStatusUI.cs script updates the rover information on both interfaces. The MissionPlanningUI.cs script also synchronizes task selections between desktop and VR controls.

Both interfaces include mission-planning controls and an Assign Mission button.

docs.title: 🔮 Future Improvements
docs.text:
• Continue improving the user interface.
  • Enhance the display of rover information.
  • Improve the overall user experience.
  • Expand interface functionality as the project develops.

docs.title: 🥽 VR Headset Integration
docs.text: The project includes VR support using the Meta Quest 3S headset. Unity uses OpenXR and the XR Interaction Toolkit to support the VR environment and interactions.

docs.title: 🎥 VR Camera Setup
docs.text: The VR camera is configured through the XR Origin in Unity. This allows the user to view the lunar environment through the VR headset.

docs.title: 📊 VR Heads-Up Display (HUD)
docs.text:
The VR HUD displays important rover information, including:

  • Position: Rover X, Y, and Z coordinates.
  • Speed: Rover speed in meters per second.
  • Heading: Rover direction in degrees.
  • Battery: Rover battery voltage.

The ROSHUD.cs script updates the information displayed on the VR HUD. If information is unavailable, the display shows N/A.

docs.title: 🎮 VR Controller and UI Interaction
docs.text:
The VR interface includes mission-planning controls for selecting tasks:

  • Find Water
  • Collect Water
  • Deposit Water
  • Return to Base

The MissionPlanningUI.cs script connects the desktop and VR task toggles. When a task is selected on either interface, the selection is synchronized with the other interface.

The VR interface also includes an assigned-tasks display and an Assign Mission button connected to the mission assignment function.

docs.title: 🔮 Future Improvements
docs.text:
• Continue improving the VR experience.
  • Enhance the user interface and overall usability.
  • Improve integration between VR components and the lunar environment.
  • Expand VR functionality as the project develops.
  • Continue testing and refining the VR system.

docs.text:

docs.title: ◈ Unity Digital Twin
docs.text: The Unity Digital Twin represents the lunar environment in a virtual 3D space. It provides the terrain and environment where the rover operates.

docs.title: ◈ Lunar Environment
docs.text:
The project uses Cesium for Unity to display the lunar surface. The LunarSouthPole_Cesium scene contains the lunar terrain and environment objects.

The Cesium Georeference component defines the geographic origin of the virtual environment.

docs.title: ⬡ Terrain and Collision
docs.text:
The lunar surface is provided through a Cesium 3D Tileset.

The following settings are important for the environment:

  • Cesium ion Asset ID: 2684829
  • Maximum Screen Space Error: 16
  • Maximum Simultaneous Tile Loads: 20
  • Maximum Cached Bytes: 536870912
  • Create Physics Meshes: Enabled

The Create Physics Meshes setting allows Cesium to generate physics meshes for terrain interaction.

docs.title: ▣ Environmental Assets
docs.text:
The environment includes objects that help represent a lunar exploration area, such as:

  • Lunar rocks and boulders
  • Base camp structures
  • Solar panels
  • Charging station structures
  • Water storage structures and platforms

These objects help create a more complete lunar environment for the digital twin.

docs.title: ✓ Testing and Validation
docs.text:
The digital environment should be checked to ensure:

  • The lunar terrain loads correctly.
  • Environmental objects appear in the scene.
  • Terrain physics meshes are generated.
  • Environment objects are positioned correctly.
  • The scene works in Play Mode.

docs.title: ✧ Future Improvements
docs.text: Possible improvements include adding more lunar surface details, improving environmental object placement, and testing terrain collision across different areas of the lunar surface.

docs.title: ⚙ Rover Physics
docs.text: The rover physics system controls how the rover moves and interacts with the lunar environment. It uses Unity's Rigidbody physics system and custom C# scripts to control movement and monitor terrain conditions.

docs.title: ⚙ Rigidbody and Lunar Gravity
docs.text:
The FlexiRover_Controller uses a Rigidbody component to manage its physical movement.

The current Rigidbody configuration includes:

  • Mass: 1.897
  • Use Gravity: Enabled

The project uses lunar gravity instead of Earth's standard gravity.

  • Gravity X: 0
  • Gravity Y: -1.62
  • Gravity Z: 0

This represents the Moon's approximate gravitational acceleration of 1.62 m/s².

docs.title: ⌘ Rover Movement and Controls
docs.text:
The MecanumRoverController script manages rover movement using keyboard input and Rigidbody velocity.

The current controls are:

Key Function W Move forward S Move backward A Move left D Move right Q Rotate left E Rotate right

The script also animates the four wheel meshes to represent rover movement.

docs.title: ⬡ Rover Collider
docs.text:
The rover has a chassis collider using a Box Collider component.

This collider helps the rover interact physically with the environment. The collider should be tested to make sure the rover does not pass through the lunar surface or other objects.

docs.title: ◉ Ground Detection and Terrain Monitoring
docs.text:
The RoverTerrainMonitor script checks the terrain underneath the rover using downward physics raycasts.

It calculates the ground slope and updates the rover's status.

The current slope thresholds are:

  • Normal: Below 10°
  • Caution: From 10° to below 15°
  • Warning: 15° or higher

The results are displayed through the rover's desktop and VR interface.

docs.title: ⌖ Obstacle Monitoring and Warning System
docs.text:
The RoverObstacleMonitor script provides obstacle monitoring.

The RoverWarningManager collects information from the terrain and obstacle monitoring scripts and displays warnings through the desktop and VR interfaces.

The current warning thresholds include:

  • Slope caution: 10°
  • Slope warning: 15°
  • Obstacle caution: 10 meters
  • Obstacle warning: 5 meters

The warning manager prioritizes more serious warnings when multiple conditions are detected.

docs.title: ✓ Testing and Validation
docs.text:
The rover physics system should be tested to verify:

  • The rover responds to keyboard controls.
  • The rover moves and rotates correctly.
  • Wheel animations respond to movement.
  • Lunar gravity affects the rover.
  • The chassis collider interacts with the terrain.
  • Ground detection reports terrain conditions.
  • Warning messages appear when required.

docs.title: ✧ Future Improvements
docs.text: Possible improvements include refining rover movement, improving terrain interaction, testing rover stability on slopes, and validating obstacle detection.
